transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-27 10:00 AM PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Carlos Mejia (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Helmsman, Cloud Architect), Samir Patel (Helmsman, Security Lead), Maya Cho (Helmsman, Platform Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
Helmsman is evaluating Redwood for private VPC/on-prem style deployment. Primary concerns: network peering/topology, private endpoints, region gating and data residency (UK/EU), egress IPs and firewall rules, and whether Dedicated reserved capacity or a private Redwood control plane inside their VPC is required. Next steps: security docs and region capability map; follow-up deep dive to validate peering and perform a quick connectivity test.

Topics discussed:
- Deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC)
- VPC peering, PrivateLink/private endpoints, Transit Gateway vs Peering
- Egress constraints and static IPs for allowlisting
- Data residency / region gating (EU/UK restriction)
- Operational concerns: runbooks, auditing and SIEM integration

Transcript body:
[00:00] Carlos (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick intro from our side, I'm Carlos, account exec, and Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Lena (Helmsman): Hey hi, Lena here. We're mostly interested in private deployment options. We run everything in a locked-down VPC and we need the inference plane to not traverse the public internet.
[00:16] Priya (Redwood): Great, that lines up with what Redwood Private can do. Just to set context, do you have a preferred cloud provider and rough region footprint?
[00:24] Lena: Primary is GCP in europe-west2, we also have a secondary on AWS eu-west-1 for DR. We have regulatory requirement to keep data in EU/UK for certain datasets.
[00:34] Samir (Helmsman): And from security we're going to need SAML SSO, audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and KMS integration. Also static egress IPs for allowlisting — our perimeter firewall doesn't like ephemeral IPs.
[00:48] Carlos: Yep, all common asks. Priya will walk through the technical variants but at a high level Redwood offers three modes: hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private (control plane in our infra or your VPC with private endpoints).
[01:02] Priya: Quick clarifying q: when you say private endpoints, do you mean PrivateLink-style endpoints inside your VPC, or full overlay where Redwood runtime is run inside your environment?
[01:10] Lena: Ideally we want endpoints in our VPC so traffic never leaves the Helmsman network. We might consider a full private runtime later but first step is private endpoints and peering to Redwood hub.
[01:20] Maya (Helmsman): Also curious about latency — we run low-latency routes for chat assistants so if there's extra hops through transit gateway it can add jitter.
[01:29] Priya: Understood. For private endpoints we support provider-managed private endpoints that terminate into our service endpoints in the region. There are two patterns: peering to a Redwood VPC with PrivateLink/Endpoint services, or running a customer-hosted runtime inside your VPC which we call Redwood Private On-Prem. The peering path can be via VPC peering or Transit Gateway depending on scale.
[01:50] Samir: If we do peering, how do we handle egress — like, what IP addresses do we give to our security team to allowlist?
[01:58] Priya: Good question — for peering/prefix routes we can provide a small set of stable egress IPs per region for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private On-Prem where the runtime lives in your VPC, egress IPs are whatever you control. There's sometimes confusion — KV cache and session state live on the runtime; if runtime is outside your VPC, we do prefix NAT and expose a small set of egress addresses.
[02:21] Lena: You said KV cash — did you mean cache?
[02:24] Priya: Yup, sorry, KV cache. Transcription folks.
[02:28] Carlos: Also to call out, for compliance we support shipping audit logs — you can pull logs via S3 or we can push to your SIEM via connector. We'll include the runbook for log forwarding.
[02:40] Lena: Good. On the region gating piece — we need the trained embedding index and inference compute to stay in eu-west-2 for a subset of traffic. Can you guarantee that?
[02:52] Priya: We have region pinning at the route level. When you create the model route you can pin model version to region and we will only route requests to capacity in that region; if capacity is constrained we can failover to a different region only if you enable fallback. For strict residency you would disable cross-region fallback.
[03:10] Maya: What about multi-cloud? We run DR on AWS, do you support a cross-cloud peering?
[03:16] Priya: Yes. You can peer AWS<->GCP to Redwood VPCs. If you want private endpoints in both clouds, we can create endpoints per cloud region. The tricky bit is ensuring consistent egress IPs for allowlisting across clouds — sometimes teams put a NAT in front to normalize egress.
[03:33] Samir: We use a third-party perimeter firewall (FortiGate) and will need to see the IP ranges. Also need assurance on TLS termination — do you terminate TLS in Redwood control plane?
[03:44] Carlos: TLS is end-to-end. For private endpoint peering TLS terminates at the service endpoint inside the Redwood VPC; for an on-prem runtime you hold certs. We can also integrate with your KMS for key material if you run private.
[03:58] Lena: Okay, can you quickly sketch the data path for the two approaches?
[04:02] Priya: Sure — handing off to quick sketch: Option A: Private endpoints/peering to Redwood-managed runtime. You establish VPC peering or Transit Gateway to Redwood VPC. Traffic hits private endpoint, traverses peering link to Redwood runtime in the same cloud region, model runs, tokens and KV cache handled by Redwood runtime. Egress IPs provided by Redwood NAT. Option B: Customer-hosted runtime (Redwood Private): we ship a runtime image, it runs in your VPC or on-prem, control plane optionally sits in Redwood's control plane with an encrypted control channel, or you can opt to host control plane as well in your VPC. No external egress needed except for optional metrics/log shipping.
[04:45] Maya: If we host the runtime, does the control plane still need to talk back to Redwood?
[04:50] Priya: You can choose a 'private control plane' where the control plane API is in a customer network — that eliminates most calls outbound. We do require a bootstrap connection for updates unless you opt for air-gapped. We have an on-prem package for that flow.
[05:03] Samir: What about performance tuning: batching and the KV cache you mentioned. How is that impacted when runtime is outside Redwood cluster?
[05:11] Priya: If runtime is in your VPC, batching and KV cache behave the same as in our hosted environment because it's the same runtime. The only difference is networking latency between your app and the runtime. That's why we recommend colocating the runtime in the same region and AZ as the callers.
[05:27] Lena: For ACLs — we use very strict NACLs. Is there a minimal set of ports/protocols we need to open?
[05:33] Priya: Mostly TCP for gRPC/HTTPS on TLS. We'll provide a minimal port matrix. For peering you'll need to accept certain prefixes and routes; for Transit Gateway there's an extra step for route tables. We'll send a port/route checklist.
[05:47] Carlos: I also want to call out quotas and rate limiting. If you put throughput behind the peering link, you may need to account for connection limits. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity with SLA to avoid throttling.
[05:58] Maya: How does Dedicated compare price-wise vs private-hosted?
[06:02] Carlos: Dedicated is a Redwood-managed reserved pool in our infra — cheaper ops for you but data flows through Redwood infrastructure. Private-hosted is you pay for infra and manage network but gives full control. We'll share a price delta spreadsheet — Priya will drop the numbers.
[06:14] Priya: I'll prepare a rough delta later today.
[06:17] Samir: On the security compliance side we need to run a vulnerability scan on any images you ship for the runtime. Are runtime images signed?
[06:26] Priya: Yes, runtime images are signed — and we can provide SBOM and vulnerability scan reports. For customers who run their own runtime we recommend you run an additional internal scan; we can also provide an attestation.
[06:38] Lena: There's also procurement constraints — we need an enterprise contract with data residency clauses and indemnities. Who do we talk to?
[06:45] Carlos: Our commercial team will loop in legal — I'll include our standard enterprise addendum, and we can highlight residency clauses. That'll be in the package I send.
[06:54] Maya: One operational question: how do upgrades happen for a customer-hosted runtime?
[07:00] Priya: We have a controlled rollout process: we produce a signed artifact, you can opt into automatic updates or manual approval. Rollouts can be canaryed across nodes; we also support A/B traffic splitting if you run multiple runtime versions.
[07:14] Samir: For observability we need trace correlation and per-request IDs so our SIEM can stitch requests back to user IDs.
[07:21] Priya: We emit trace headers and request IDs; we can forward them with logs and provide a tracing hook. We'll add the sample tracing config to the runbook.
[07:31] Lena: Let's talk about our DR model — during failover we may redirect some traffic to our AWS DR region. If Redwood region is eu-west-2 and you don't have capacity there, I don't want silent routing to US. How are failovers surfaced?
[07:44] Priya: We surface failover behavior in the route configuration. By default some customers enable automatic fallback, but for strict residency you would disable fallback and instead surface explicit error. Alternatively you can create an exception route for DR traffic that goes to a pinned region in AWS. We'll walk through route policies in the next session.
[08:05] Carlos: Quick poll — is the team leaning toward peering-first or hosting runtime in-house as the long-term plan?
[08:12] Lena: Short-term peering with private endpoints to prove connectivity. Long-term possible on-prem/private runtime to avoid egress.
[08:20] Maya: Agreed. We want to run a pilot with a few endpoints and then measure latency and cost.
[08:25] Samir: Also want to do a security review — can you provide SOC2 and any ISO certs you have?
[08:31] Carlos: Yes, SOC2 report and ISO certs. I'll attach them to the follow-up email.
[08:36] Lena: For the pilot we need to know the expected token throughput — can Redwood give us guidance on instance sizing for our expected QPS?
[08:44] Priya: Absolutely — share your current QPS, avg seq len, and concurrency targets and we'll map to a recommended profile (GPU type, batch config, quantization). We'll include a sizing worksheet.
[08:56] Maya: We'll put together a quick traffic profile doc.
[09:00] Priya: One last nuts-and-bolts: when you set up VPC peering to a Redwood VPC, you must ensure route propagation for the prefixes we provide. For Transit Gateway there's a slightly different setup and you can do centralized egress. If you're using cloud express connectivity (Interconnect / Direct Connect), that also works through transit.
[09:18] Lena: We're on GCP Interconnect for our onprem -> cloud. Do you support partner interconnect routes?
[09:23] Priya: Yes, Partner Interconnect is fine as long as the route reaches your VPC — it's just the regular IP reachability. We'll work with your network team to validate.
[09:32] Samir: A question about secrets — if we have to pass keys to the runtime, do we want Redwood to manage them or do we hold them in our KMS?
[09:40] Priya: If you're running runtime in your VPC you can host keys; for Redwood-managed runtime we offer KMS integrations and envelope encryption so you retain control over keys in your KMS. We'll add a doc on KMS integration patterns.
[09:52] Carlos: Alright, looks like good alignment. Quick recap of next steps: I'll send security docs and legal starter packet; Priya will send region capacity and price delta; Lena will share network diagram and traffic profile; we schedule a tech deep dive next week.
[10:08] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks Carlos and Priya.
[10:11] Carlos: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of transcript.
